what_is_closed: A constructive source-normalized decaying-mode witness along beta=-1+epsilon and zeta=sqrt(epsilon) has unit amplitude and unit principal-mode norm, while its 30-component boundary-data vector has only two nonzero entries r with r=[(9*sqrt(2)+5*sqrt(6))/12]*epsilon+O(epsilon^2). Therefore the Kreiss constant cannot be bounded uniformly over the entire negative subluminal shift family as beta approaches -1; under the declared Euclidean source norms K_beta >= (9-5*sqrt(3))/epsilon+O(1).

The witness is non-degenerate for every epsilon>0 and is cross-checked against the registered source-basis boundary matrix. This is a family-uniformity no-go, not a failure of the fixed-beta Kreiss condition.
what_remains_open: Rinne's per-fixed-shift, frequency-uniform Kreiss result is not refuted; the bound may depend on the fixed background shift. Uniform estimates on compact shift ranges and the beta-to-zero transition remain to be checked separately.
Closed frequency-boundary behavior, variable-coefficient/nonlinear GH, non-periodic full CPBC evolution, dimensional gravitational observables, and the curved 3+1 parent gate remain open.
